prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: It depends on your trip. Airbnb is best for unique stays, local hosts, and flexible/longer stays; Vrbo is usually best for whole-home family or group rentals; Booking.com is strongest for hotels and instant bookings (and many apartments) with easier cancellations and 24/7 support. Use the one that fits the type of accommodation you want, then follow a host-quality checklist below.

Which platform when (quick guide)
- Airbnb — wide variety (private rooms, shared, entire homes, unique stays). Good for local hosts, experiences, and month+ stays. Has “Superhost,” ID verification, and AirCover protection.
- Vrbo — focused on whole-home rentals, usually owner-hosted and family-friendly (pool, big houses). Good for groups and longer family trips.
- Booking.com — strong for hotels, many instant-book apartments; good for last-minute and flexible cancellation options. Little host interaction; best if you prefer hotel-style service or instant confirmation.
- Tip: Compare the same property across platforms (sometimes different fees/prices) and always check total price (cleaning fee, service fee, taxes).

How to find a good host — practical checklist
1. Read reviews carefully
   - Prioritize recent reviews (last 6–12 months).
   - Look for comments about cleanliness, accuracy of listing, check-in process, responsiveness, and neighborhood.
   - Watch for repeated complaints, not just single isolated issues.

2. Check host signals
   - High response rate and quick replies.
   - “Superhost”/“Premier Host”/“Top Host” badges are useful but read reviews too.
   - Host’s profile: verified ID, photos, and a detailed bio are good signs.
   - Number of listings: one-off owners often offer more personal service than large management companies (but companies may be more consistent).

3. Inspect the listing closely
   - Accurate, plentiful photos (especially of sleeping areas and bathrooms).
   - Clear description of amenities, rules, and fees (cleaning fee, pet fees, security deposit).
   - Up-to-date calendar and clear cancellation policy.
   - Exact location or neighborhood info; use map view to confirm proximity to transit/attractions.

4. Communicate before booking
   - Ask specific questions: arrival/check-in, parking, Wi‑Fi speed, noise, heating/AC, number of beds, and anything critical to you (workspace, accessibility).
   - Request photos of anything not shown (crib, workspace, parking spot).
   - Good hosts answer within a day and provide helpful details.

5. Watch for red flags
   - Requests to pay or communicate off-platform.
   - Vague or inconsistent listing details.
   - Very low price with few/no reviews or stock photos.
   - Host unwilling to confirm simple details.

6. Verify neighborhood safety and logistics
   - Check Google Maps/Street View, distance to transit, noise (near bars/airport), and local short-term rental rules (some cities have bans).

7. Protect yourself
   - Always pay through the platform (for refunds and support).
   - Check cancellation policy and consider travel insurance for non-refundable stays.
   - Note the platform’s protections (Airbnb AirCover, Vrbo Book with Confidence, Booking.com support).

Sample pre-booking message (copy/paste and tweak)
Hi, I’m [Name]. I’m planning to stay from [dates]. A few quick questions: what is the check-in process? Is parking available? Is Wi‑Fi fast enough for video calls? Are the bed sizes accurate? Are there any building rules or notable house rules I should know? Thanks!

Day-of-arrival checklist
- Confirm check-in code/meeting time the day before.
- Get important details saved (Wi‑Fi, host phone, emergency contacts).
- Take photos of any pre-existing damage on arrival.

If something goes wrong
- Message host first with photos and a clear request.
- If unresolved, use the platform’s support/dispute process and keep all messages in-platform.

Which platform I’d pick for common situations
- Solo traveler / short city trip: Airbnb or Booking.com (depends if you want a local host vs instant booking).
- Family / big group / whole house needed: Vrbo or Airbnb whole-home listings.
- Hotel-style service or last-minute booking: Booking.com.
- Long-term stay (30+ days): Airbnb (monthly discounts) or local rental sites; check local taxes and regulations.

If you want, tell me: destination, travel dates, party size, and priorities (budget, privacy, parking, workspace, pet-friendly). I can recommend which platform and give search/filter tips for that trip.
